calls.head: The Flyers roll four lines; the Devils lean on their top six
calls.body: On depth, Philadelphia is one of the league’s best and New Jersey is one of the league’s worst. That’s about as far apart as two teams get.
calls.call: The Flyers spread their forward ice time deeper down the lineup than the Devils.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 1 and 0 games this season
calls.happened: On bottom-six share of forward ice time, Philadelphia had 42% and New Jersey 39%. Coming in, Philadelphia was at 43% and New Jersey at 40%.

calls.head: The Flyers hit; the Devils mostly don’t
calls.body: On physicality, Philadelphia is one of the league’s best and New Jersey is one of the league’s worst. That’s about as far apart as two teams get.
calls.call: The Flyers hit more than the Devils in the close stretches of the game.

calls.happened: On hit score in close games (arena-adjusted, 100 is league average), Philadelphia had hit score 124 and New Jersey hit score 88. Coming in, Philadelphia was at hit score 116 and New Jersey at hit score 85.

NJD.head: We gave New Jersey a 64% chance, and New Jersey delivered.

PHI.head: We gave Philadelphia only a 36% chance, and it went the way we feared.

surprises.head: Philadelphia couldn’t get good looks
surprises.body: Philadelphia’s shots at 5-on-5 were less dangerous than usual: a 4.1% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.4% (league average 6.3%). A team strays this far about once every 40 games.

surprises.head: Philadelphia tried a different line
surprises.body: M. Michkov, N. Cates, T. Foerster played 7:52 together at 5-on-5, a trio that isn’t one of Philadelphia’s usual lines.

story.head: Hughes wins it in overtime
paras: Rasmus Ristolainen opened the scoring midway through the first. Twice the Devils answered a Flyers lead. Jack Hughes won it in overtime.
The score was fair. Replay this game’s chances a hundred times and the Devils win nine in ten. The Flyers tried a line they hadn’t used before: Matvei Michkov, Noah Cates and Tyson Foerster.

items.text: Whether the Flyers keep that line together at home against Carolina on Saturday.
Both of the preview’s calls held.
